items.title: Harold Ousley interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001
items.q: In fact I worked with Sunnyland and Memphis Slim, Roosevelt Sykes.

ctx.x: Was there a separate blues scene also at that time? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-

Yeah. There was a club on 47th Street. I think at the Club 409. The people like Muddy Water, Sunnyland Slim, used to work there. I’d go by there and hear everybody. In fact I worked with Sunnyland and Memphis Slim, Roosevelt Sykes. Because in Chicago a lot of times if musicians wanted to work regular you had to work with blues groups, you know what I mean. So I got the opportunity, which was very good, because you add to your repertoire and your ability. And of course the blues is one of the centerpieces of the…
Good statement. Probably you ran into circumstances playing in some new keys I would imagine, if you started playing with guitar players?
